symptom: `go mod tidy` could not run in the repo at all: "finding module for package github.com/mendixlabs/mxcli/mdl/backend/mpr ... no matching versions for query latest". Surfaced while dropping the v1 BSON driver from go.mod, which needs tidy; the workaround was `go mod edit -droprequire` plus hand-pruning go.sum
cause: mdl/exprcheck/roundtrip_test.go imported three things that no longer exist: mdl/backend/mpr (the legacy engine, deleted), executor.GetHierarchyForMining and executor.DescribeMicroflowToString. It never failed a build because it sat behind `//go:build roundtrip` — a tag NO Makefile target and no CI job ever passes, and the only file in the tree that uses it. go mod tidy considers every build tag, so it was the one command that still saw the file
file: `mdl/exprcheck/roundtrip_test.go` deleted; ported to `mdl/executor/exprcheck_roundtrip_test.go` under the `integration` tag
insight: A build tag nothing runs is not a disabled test, it is a deleted test that still looks present — `grep -rl 'go:build <tag>'` returning exactly one file, with no Makefile target naming that tag, is the signal. This one rotted through the legacy-engine deletion AND two executor API removals without a single red build, and the only thing that ever noticed was `go mod tidy`, whose failure reads as a module-resolution problem rather than a dead test. So when tidy complains about a package that was deliberately deleted, look for a test behind an orphan tag, not for a dependency problem. Porting beat deleting: the assertion (describe every microflow, re-parse each expression, expect zero hints from the robust parser) covers grammar gaps the unit tests cannot, since they only feed the parser expressions someone thought to write. Port target is `package executor` under the `integration` tag, where setupTestEnv/describeMDL already provide the real-project harness and `make test-integration-executor` actually runs it; the import cycle the original file's header warned about does not arise in that direction, because mdl/exprcheck does not import mdl/executor. The removed executor.GetHierarchyForMining is replaced by building the containerID->module-name map from backend.ListModules(). Two vacuity guards matter here because the fixture project lives in a separate repo (mx-test-projects/) and TestMain SKIPS the whole suite when it is absent: assert the microflow count is non-zero and the expression-slot count is non-zero, or an empty fixture passes silently. After the port, `go mod tidy` ran clean and pruned 35 more stale go.sum lines than the hand-edit had
